headline: Southborough boards set positions for the October Special Town Meeting, narrowed Neary School renovation options, and opened hearings on a proposed Costco.
synopsis: Town boards focused heavily in September on finalizing warrant articles for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, revealing sharp divisions between committees on key funding proposals. The Select Board and the Advisory Committee split on CPA funding articles for Southborough Golf Club irrigation and a Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge, as well as a proposed zoning amendment for two-family dwellings. In school planning, the Elementary School Building Committee eliminated an exterior addition concept for Neary Elementary School to focus on interior courtyard renovations and a $15 million baseline repair scope. The Planning Board opened public hearings on a proposal to build a 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position gas station on Coslin Drive. Municipal departments also prepared dual FY28 budget submissions to model the potential impact of an override failure at the spring Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Project Options Narrowed
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate Option 4 and focus design and estimating efforts on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline.
top_items.body: Preliminary cost estimates presented by consultants ranged from $24.4 million to $49.2 million across design options, including an estimated $4.5 million roof replacement. Architects advised that Option 4, which proposed an exterior gym addition, faced severe site challenges from high groundwater and unsuitable soils. The committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 and voted 4-0 to instruct designers to focus on interior courtyard renovations and a scoped $15 million baseline ahead of a multi-board review.

top_items.title: Planning Board Opens Review of Coslin Drive Costco
top_items.why: Costco Wholesale presented site and traffic plans for a proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-pump gas station on Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: The development team presented civil engineering, grading, stormwater management, and traffic modeling for the 26.12-acre parcel straddling the Southborough and Westborough town border. Residents and board members raised concerns regarding traffic congestion along Route 9, cut-through traffic on Flagg Road, and truck turnaround movements at Route 85. The Planning Board continued the public hearing to October 19, 2026.

top_items.title: Boards Divide on Two-Family Housing Zoning Article
top_items.why: The Select Board recommended approving a zoning amendment for two-family dwellings, while the Advisory Committee voted against supporting it.
top_items.body: Sponsored by the Zoning Board of Appeals, Article 2 removes a two-year waiting period to convert existing single-family homes into two-family dwellings and regulates conversions and new construction by special permit. The Select Board voted 4-1 (and later 5-0 on revised text) to recommend the article to encourage housing variety, but the Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending it due to concerns over density, municipal service burdens, and septic capacity. The Planning Board continued its public hearing on the bylaw to the morning of Town Meeting on October 17.

top_items.title: Committees Split on $433,546 Golf Irrigation Funding
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted unanimously against recommending $433,546 in CPA funds for golf course irrigation, despite support from the Select Board and CPC.
top_items.body: The project to replace the failing irrigation system at the Southborough Golf Club has risen to an estimated cost of $1,087,296 after initial bids exceeded original estimates. Although the Community Preservation Committee voted 4-1 and the Select Board voted 5-0 to support the warrant article combining CPA funds with $100,000 from the golf revolving fund, the Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against it, maintaining that course capital improvements should be funded by user fees rather than town CPA balances.

top_items.title: Select Board and Advisory Oppose Peninsula Trail Bridge
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 1-4 and the Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against supporting $217,318 in additional CPA funding for a pedestrian footbridge.
top_items.body: The Southborough Trails Committee requested supplementary CPA funds to install a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge on the Framingham border, bringing the total estimated project cost to $428,550 after earlier bids exceeded original appropriations. While the Community Preservation Committee supported the article 5-0, both the Select Board and Advisory Committee voted not to recommend approval, citing municipal budget pressures and high costs. In response, the Trails Committee discussed public outreach and plans to seek an extension of existing CPA funds to December 2029.

top_items.title: Departments Model Dual FY28 Budgets for Override
top_items.why: Town administration directed departments to submit two FY28 budget models to account for the outcome of a planned spring tax override ballot question.
top_items.body: Budget A reflects a level-service budget that accommodates a 5 percent total wage adjustment approved by the Personnel Board. Budget B assumes an override failure and requires a zero-percent increase over FY27 appropriations. Department heads across the Library, Health Department, and Conservation Commission reported that Budget B would force severe operational reductions, including eliminated programming, reduced staff working hours, and slashed professional training.

top_items.title: Select Board Recommits to Regional Waste Consortium
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to continue participating in a 35-community consortium to negotiate regional refuse disposal rates with WIN Waste.
top_items.body: Southborough has participated in the Walpole-led municipal group since 2006 to negotiate bulk disposal rates at the Millbury waste-to-energy incinerator. The board evaluated town counsel concerns regarding shared legal representation against the pricing power of the 35-member block, voting 5-0 to stay in the consortium ahead of the current disposal agreement's expiration on December 31, 2027.
